headline: Leasing strength and acquisitions lift FFO, guidance raised
summary_short: Simon's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,791M (+19.5% y/y, +1.9% q/q), partly from consolidating a previously unconsolidated joint-venture stake, while Real Estate FFO per share grew 7.9% y/y to $3.29 and diluted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.70 on a one-time prior-year investment gain.
summary_long: Revenue rose 19.5% y/y and 1.9% q/q to $1,791M, aided by the prior-year TRG equity investment becoming consolidated plus broad-based leasing demand, accelerating traffic, and retailer sales growth (sales per sq ft +13.9% y/y; base minimum rent +6.3% y/y; occupancy flat at 96.0%). Domestic property NOI grew 8.5% y/y. Diluted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.70 because Q2 2025 included a $0.21 non-cash gain from investment activity; excluding that, results improved. The company completed $1.4B of secured loans, a €500M senior notes offering, and a $460M term loan, lifting long-term debt 13.0% y/y to $28,700M while cash rose to $1,019M. Simon repurchased $211.4M of stock and raised full-year 2026 Real Estate FFO per share guidance to $13.20-$13.30 from $13.10-$13.25.

drivers.explanation: Consolidation of the previously equity-method TRG investment following an October 31, 2025 transaction, plus broad-based leasing demand, accelerating traffic, and retailer sales growth; domestic property NOI grew 8.5% y/y.
Diluted EPS fell y/y only because the year-ago quarter included a $0.21 per-share non-cash after-tax investment gain; the release notes no similar item this quarter.

Equity fell versus Q1 as $211.4M of quarterly buybacks and dividends reduced it; it remains far above the prior year, which predates the TRG transaction's consolidation onto the balance sheet.
Share count declined as Simon repurchased 793,077 common shares and 237,618 OP units during the quarter at an average $205.10 per share/unit.

Management credits the quarter to steady leasing demand, rising foot traffic, higher retailer sales, and contributions from last year's acquisitions; full-year Real Estate FFO per share guidance was raised again.
